# Journey & game design

[Wiki home](README.md) | [Edit source](../../AGENTS.md)

## Gameplan (2026-10-13, from issue #72; design reference since 2026-10-17: `Assets/Design/DESIGN.md`)

**Direction 2026-10-17 (DESIGN.md "Gameplan"):** one continuous co-op journey, no roguelite runs and no time loop. Progress = upgrading the ships and the warp drive. Open world: the scanner shows every site (ore to ruins) and the Nostos' board computer highlights what is interesting or needed, without missions; flying there, landing, disembarking, harvesting and carrying the loot back are played in the world. A failed landing costs what the landing party carried, the landed ship stays as a salvageable wreck (#132). The Rift (#81) and the time loop are gone (code removed in #145). Progression has two layers: the players' own crew ships (classes Dart -> heavy fighter -> multi-crew frigate, no freighters, #113) and the Nostos as shared base, scanner platform and jump ship whose upgrades (warp drive first) open further areas. Galaxies can be revisited (#142), every ship has utility slots for mining lasers/drones (#143), the character grows only through equipment (#58, no skill tree), the journey save belongs to the crew and any member can host (#144), and the board computer (#140) is sarcastic but helpful. Not built yet (the text below describes what exists today): down/revive and the failed landing (#146), the open-world scanner and board computer (#128, #140), crew ship classes and modules.
The game is now a **journey home**: a moon mission (*SELENE-4*) on its return flight to Earth (the family watches it live on the news, #109) is swallowed by an anomaly/wormhole, the crew wakes in M33 and flies through 5 Local Group galaxies (M33 -> M31 -> NGC 6822 -> Leo I -> LMC) home to Sol, upgrading the **warp drive** (Mk I-V, Home Drive) to shrink the **Home ETA**. Travel = flown warp flights (#73). Failing: no game over and no time loop since #145 (the time loop of #86 and the Rift of #81 were removed; #132/#146 add down/revive and the failed landing). Gameplay core planned in #128 (scanner and sites, coordinate fragments -> drive core), #129 (special sites with a structure, per-planet alert level), #130 (every pilot flies their own ship inside the warp bubble, multi-seat = gunner/engineer), #131 (drive variants with trade-offs). Enemies: nature + aliens only (no pirates); Wardens = alien guardian species (#42). The Collapse/Rift is gone. Credits -> Salvage (`NetInventory.Salvage`), Stardust -> Memory fragments (`Meta.Data.Memories`), done in #112.
- **Gameplay decisions follow `Assets/Design/DESIGN.md` "Gameplan: The Journey Home" and the open issues in roadmap #53, not the legacy code** (#72, the original gameplan issue, is closed; "part of #72" in issues is history). #46 (run structure: 5 galaxies, systems, galaxy map, suspend save; gates/Collapse removed) is in. #73 is split into #78 (crew warp drive), #79 (flown warp), #80 (cruise, hops) and #81 (finale), all done. #74 is split into #86 (time loop, built then removed in #145), #87 (prologue: playable return flight from the Moon, anomaly, waking in M33), #109 (story intro: family watching the news, TV -> cockpit, "SIGNAL LOST"), #88 (homecoming: Sol, landing on Earth, closing news scene, credits), #132/#145/#146 (failing without a time loop) and #89 (lore), in that order (sub-issues of #74). #49 is now only the home ship *Nostos* (the SELENE-4 mission ship, built from the Ark); small ships moved to #113. #108 (done) replaced the warp button/countdown: every hop and galaxy warp starts seamlessly by flying out of a jump zone at the system edge (Galactic Rim + skip zone only in a galaxy's outermost system). The flight home from the LMC is the longest warp flight (#81); still legacy until their issues land: the homecoming result screen instead of the Earth/Moon approach and landing (#88), the intro cinematic (once per player) instead of the prologue (#87) and pirates (#51). The home ship *Nostos* is in (#49). Energy Cells are gone (#78: Exotic Matter, item id `exotic`).
